content_html:
The Mountain of 7 Colors, or Vinicunca, is one of the most impressive destinations in Peru. Located more than 5,000 meters above sea level, this natural wonder has become a must-see for travelers visiting Cusco. However, the altitude and road conditions can make the experience challenging. Here we give you all the tips to enjoy it to the fullest and avoid problems in the attempt.

1. How to get to the Mountain of 7 Colors?

From Cusco, the trip is divided into three parts:

  1. Car trip: You take transportation to the community of Cusipata, which takes approximately 2 hours.
  2. Path to the starting point: From Cusipata, continue by car 40 more minutes to the starting point of the walk.
  3. Trekking to the top: The walk is 4km (one way) with a progressive ascent to the 5,036 m.a.s.l.. Depending on the pace, it takes between 1.5 and 2.5 hours.

If you don't feel safe walking the entire route, you can rent a horse with local residents for most of the route (except the last 300 meters).

2. Altitude: the biggest challenge

The height is the biggest challenge when visiting Vinicunca. altitude sickness (soroche) can cause headache, fatigue, dizziness, and lack of oxygen. To avoid it:

  • Prior acclimatization: Stay in Cusco at least 2 days before to get used to the height.
  • Constant hydration: Drink plenty of water before and during the walk.
  • Avoid heavy foods and alcohol: The days before, opt for light meals.
  • Bring coca leaves or muña candies: They help relieve the symptoms of altitude sickness.
  • Take your time: Walk at a slow pace and rest when you need to.

3. What is the best time to visit?

The Mountain of 7 Colors changes with the seasons, even so, never trust yourself that the climate of Cusco is uncertain.

  • Dry season (May – September): It is the best option, with clear skies and vibrant colors.
  • Rainy season (November – March): There is more mud and the mountain may be covered in snow.

The tours usually leave between 3 and 4 a.m., allowing you to arrive early and avoid the crowds.

4. What to bring?

Layered clothing: It is cold in the morning and hot at noon. Wear a thermal jacket, a windbreaker and breathable clothing.
Hat, gloves and scarf: Essential for the cold and wind.
Sunscreen and sunglasses: The radiation at this altitude is intense.
Trekking footwear: The road is uneven and can be muddy.
Energy snack: Dried fruits, granola bars or chocolates will give you energy.
Cash: To pay the entrance fee (S/ 20 Peruvians – S/ 25 foreigners) or if you want to rent a horse.

You can buy all this in Cusco at a low price.

5. Is the Mountain of 7 Colors worth visiting?

Definitely yes! Despite the physical effort, the panoramic view of the natural colors of the mountain is impressive. In addition, the tour will allow you to appreciate Andean landscapes, llamas and alpacas in their natural habitat.

With good preparation and a positive attitude, this experience will be unforgettable. Dare to conquer Vinicunca!
